## 1. The reading

- "Which" is the right core, but as drafted it decides "X's course depends on how many loose distinctions the second start knot held, given Y's members are usable". It does not yet decide "which made pattern" (see 5).
- W has no clause that tests the meeting; the timing clause is only "after, therefore through" (see 6).
- The course from X only leaves out joint births, so joining with Y, the most direct way to depend on Y, is invisible. Report FD's trace and the count of joint births beside every verdict.
- Left out of the fold: the third property entirely, and "a pattern the rules make" for Y in any strong sense (Y_h is one round of offshoots of a hand-built knot).
- "Kept" is not a fair least form. The two states already differ at t_d, so later births differ almost by implication (one more usable loose distinction gives one more offshoot). It also compares multisets, so it can say "not kept" when only incidence differs.
- Fairer least form: with everything else barred, the rosters descended from X only are not the same (SD 29–30) in each of the last k rounds read, or one has ended and the other makes a birth in round T.

## 2. Lemma L and the line

- As stated it is wrong under parity: IMPLIED tests a birth against the span of every knot's rule, Y's included, with no meeting. Add the implied flag and the guard's stop to I_t.
- I_t in the lemma is not WD 4.3's interface record (which lacks candidates' identities, groups among X's own members, and the implied flag). Two objects carry one name.
- Once I_t lists every input of the step, the lemma is true and near-tautological: a course is a function of the step's inputs. It rules out action without contact and nothing more.
- It does not dissolve the line. The brief's L2 said "does not use at that birth"; the draft refutes "never looked at", which is a different sentence.
- (a) is weak: by the lemma, "alike at the meeting, different later" only says Y's later births differ. It is a fact about Y's course, and on the made class it is nearly empty, since member counts already differ at the meeting.
- (b) is the honest form. Under a law whose every used value at one birth takes at most v values, X's course from X only separates more than v second patterns. No single value can then have handed the difference over; several births composed it.
- (b) is trivial for a pair and for count-valued inputs (ORD's demand, owing, holders). Those laws are L1 by nature and should be reported as "one value of one birth separates them".
- (c) is the third property, not the line.
- Headline: W on a births-only class, with (b) as an exclusive verdict on every case ("handed in one value" or "composed over several births"). Do not make (b) the only headline; it may be "none".

## 3. The premise against the rations

Test I would register for "the rule is not a reader":
- (i) stated with no X, Y, descent, part or name;
- (ii) uses only values the recorded round already forms at the acting knot;
- (iii) applies at every birth of every start;
- (iv) what it changes with X alone is reported, since "inert alone" marks a meeting detector, not innocence;
- (v) the number of values it can pass at one birth is stated;
- (vi) a difference that one such value separates is credited to the law.

Each member against it:
- **PARENT-OWING** passes (i) to (iii). But owing is formed from groups, at least two holder steps from the parent, not "one holder step at most". It is unbounded, and on this class it is a function of h. By (vi) it is the law handing a count over: L1, an allowed rule, not a pattern reading.
- **PARENT-OWING, round 2** (my hand reading of SD steps 1–2, to be confirmed by a listing): Y_h's members owe h−1, so under CANCEL-OFFSHOOT their offshoots receive h−1. The law stamps the start's h on Y's own line.
- **PARENT-LOOSE** copies a count unchanged from parent to offshoot: Y_h's line holds h for ever. That is a mark of descent supplied by the law. Fails "never descent" in effect.
- **TAKEN-HOLDERS** measures the other pattern's holders at the take; nearest to a reader. Keep it only as a marked comparison.
- **J-ONE-EACH** uses parts; fails (i). Make it the positive control.
- **MET-EVERY** gives the newborn every eligible place of a met knot. In the CAP-3 case X's joins hold one place per place of Y's start knot. That is arguably "handing over whole"; ask the owner before it stays in the search.
- **BY-SHORTFALL** passes.

## 4. The rules that use no names

- Lemma N looks right for the round, including same-round takes, implied births and joins of three or more: every step is defined on holders, meetings, the record and counts.
- Conditions to write in: the guard stops by counts and never alters a completed round; the wall cap is not equivariant, so cap by counts.
- WD 1.1 says "FD 2 exactly", but FD 2.4 allows at most one take per birth. State the amendment.
- The check must compare whole structures with parents, not sizes and X's course.
- "Every candidate" is a lawful rule but not a fair carrier: it piles holders, fails not-all-equal almost wherever it acts, and copies place sets.
- Fairer, in order:
  1. **Every choice read on supports**: C_a is the set of courses over all histories; the claim is that C_a and C_b are disjoint. No weighting is needed, and it covers every rule and numbering.
  2. Uniform sampled takes with the take-by-take weighting, read as distributions.
  3. A structural selector, such as every candidate with the fewest holders.

## 5. The class

- Yes: fix Y's start knot. On the made class every positive so far is consistent with "the start's h, relayed by one round of Y's births". Barred-both cannot see that.
- By my reading of SD step 1, Y_h's members are in h−1 pairs and hold 2 under FLOOR1. So Y_4 to Y_6 are all short, and under RETIRE or WAIT they make no birth after s. P3's negative is then partly implied for the FLOOR1 laws.
- Under WAIT, short members of Y still cancel X's groups. So barred-both tests "Y's members usable", not "Y's births".
- **Smallest deterministic class**: one start made-h, with second patterns Y_h^a, where a of the h members are left usable and the rest barred at s. This is the owner's with-and-without test with part of Y present.
- Run it as two factors: h (the start's) by a (acting members). A difference that follows a at fixed h is Y's births'; one that follows h at fixed a is the start's. This replaces barred-both.
- The bars are a scaffold; say so.
- **Unsupplied class**: one start, two histories that agree on every take except those of births descended from Y only before the meeting.
- "The same meeting" in both classes: the same start and names, the same linking knot or taken distinction, the same round, and the same births of X (literally, with no renaming before the first difference).

## 6. The controls

- **Barred-both** sees whether the start with Y inert gives the difference. It is empty by construction for "through the meeting": any effect of Y vanishes with Y barred, whether it came by a meeting, a third part, a closing or the guard.
- **FD 5.6's M** sees joinability only. It cannot see takes or demand-step meetings, and it leaks through "contained in no single met set". M′ sees a third part.
- **The sealed run**: drop it. Sealing X properly (X uses a structure with Y's births after s removed) is B(i) again when there are two patterns, so it is barred-both under another name.
- **The right control** is attribution, made a condition of W. At the first round where the used values differ, take the first differing value in the round's step order. It involves a knot of Y's descent (through the meeting), a knot from both or neither (third part), or an implied flag, closing or guard (round-wide, which FD 5.7 calls supplied).
- Add single-way maskings (joinability, takes, demand), reported only.

## 7. Lemmas A and P

- **A** is false as written under parity: an implied birth receives nothing, by the span. The count is a function of (p, D, implied).
- Also, p counts takes and D is read on the next roster; both depend on what is met.
- The fate is correct, sharpened: right as "never of what its parents hold loose", wrong as "never of what its parents meet".
- **P**, first sentence: holds for the three recorded treatments, fails under BY-SHORTFALL, where what a member keeps depends on its owing.
- **P**, conclusion: does not follow. PARENT-LOOSE changes the base course (offshoots that take receive h, not 1, and Y_h's line holds h), so "every case is also a case under FLOOR1" is not implied. P5 is (a), not (b).

## 8. The one case

- Do not register it as "the predicted least law". Register it as a replication of a seen case, under parity.
- The ration differs from FLOOR1 twice: a floor of 2 for offshoots that take, and the owing. Add two controls: offshoots receive a constant 2, and max(1, o). If the constant gives W, the ration's use of owing is not needed.
- It is the guard's doing if the first difference falls in the stopping round, if T differs between the pair because of the guard, or if any verdict on common rounds changes between ×1, ×10 and ×100.
- The guard's limits are not written in WD; write the numbers.
- T is 3 or 4 and t_d is 3: one round of evidence. Say it.
- Parity only does not disqualify, but it bars the unqualified sentence. Report "under parity; none under not-all-equal", and test every knot of the ×10 runs.

## 9. The cheaper route

- Yes, it would answer the brief as worded: no new rule, with ORD's demand as what is carried. It still carries the class objection of 5.
- "Every numbering on the verdicts" is sound only as set disjointness: C_a (courses over all numberings of start a) and C_b share nothing. Paired numberings impose a pairing that does not exist.
- All four parts of the verdict must be reread under each numbering, not only "differs".
- Size: numberings that differ by an automorphism of the start give identical runs. My arithmetic gives (h+3)!/(2·h!) × 2 = 120, 210, 336, 504 runs for h = 3 to 6, so every numbering is exact in seconds. The 4n + 200 sample is unnecessary.
- State it as "under take-the-oldest, whatever the numbering". The law still uses names. Only the every-choice form removes that.
- Run it first, under its own one-page frozen text, on the h-by-a class as well.

## 10. The search and the stop

- The cost is a partial order: vectors compared by component, with a last component that has no order. "First" is ambiguous (MET-EVERY/ORD against STEPS1-EVERY/PARENT-OWING are incomparable).
- Stopping at the first positive is unsound for "least", and pointless when the whole list costs 15 minutes.
- Decide every law; report the minimal laws with W as a set, "among n decided, m undecided".
- The 78 laws are not derivable from the table. Write the list out.
- "Nothing was added after" is true, but T-NONE, MET-SAMPLED and FBP were removed and J-ONE-EACH reworded. Disclose.

## 11. The definitions

- **Course from X only**: WD 4.1's parenthetical disagrees with D 2.6 on third-part parents. A hash is not a comparison; give the canonical form.
- **Interface record**: see 2. "The same up to renaming" must mean under a renaming that carries the courses.
- **Meeting round**: fine with the demand roster. Say whether joint descendants count as both.
- **"At or after both"**: require equal meeting rounds, or report the gap. Unequal rounds are a timing difference.
- **Barred-both**: compare through T, not t_d, and report "the start's, later". Rename what it tests (see 5).
- **Kept**: see 1. It needs t_d < T, so it is undecided whenever the guard stops the run.
- **Resolution**: computed on open runs it counts the start's differences. Report open, barred and net. "1 is presence at most" is wrong; 1 says nothing of presence.
- **BY-SHORTFALL**: a member that makes offshoots and keeps some does not "wait" in SD's sense.
- **TAKEN-HOLDERS**: say that only step-5′ takes count.
- **Inconsistencies**:
  - Claim section 3, section 7 item 2 and WD 5.2 still use the sealed run; section 5 does not.
  - WD 4 is numbered 5, 7, 6.
  - WD 6.2 cites a run 5 that does not exist.
  - "Run 4 with the guard ×10" is run 3 in the table.
  - P3 calls a pair "W" that the registered W excludes.

## 12. The predictions

- **True by construction or implication**: P1 (a check, fine as one); P3 in part (inert Y); "kept" in most cases.
- **Replication only**: P0, P2, P3's named pair, P4, P6.
- **Not predictions (no way to fail)**: P7, P9, P10. List them as readings. P10 is a universal that no bounded run decides. P9 is nearly empty on this class.
- **Over-pinned**: P8 (every pair, every treatment, both takes) and P4 ("every run").
- **Vague**: P11 ("many holders").
- **Missing**:
  - Positive control: J-ONE-EACH must be found by the tests.
  - Planted start's case: the CAP-3 pair must be classed "the start's".
  - Negative control: no taking rule must give one course over the class, which also exposes IMPLIED and the guard.
  - A gate for the new rules: one case listed birth by birth by hand.
  - Per law, which Y_h make any birth.

## 13. Sizes

- Not now. First count the histories of the every-choice form depth-first without reading them. D 2.7's 60,000 bound may fit the hour.
- Ask later only if route 9 survives and a seeded sample finds no shared course. A sample can refute disjointness but never confirm it.

## 14. Words

- **name-free**: replace ("free" is the glossary's). Use "a law that uses no names".
- **every candidate / a sole candidate**: keep.
- **X's own course**: replace with "the course from X only"; "course" is FD's trace.
- **sealed run**: drop with the run.
- **kept**: replace; SD has kept groups and WD 0 has "kept with their meanings". Use "lasts with the rest barred".
- **alike at the meeting**: keep, defined on the full used values.
- **needs Y's births**: replace here with "needs Y's members usable"; keep the old phrase for the h-by-a verdict.
- **interface record**: replace with "the values used at X's births".
- **resolution**: replace with "the number of distinct courses over the class".
- **Presence / Which**: use "Whether" and "Which", the guide's pair.
- **PARENT-OWING, PARENT-LOOSE, TAKEN-HOLDERS**: keep; always gloss the floor of two.
- **BY-SHORTFALL**: SHORT-BY.
- **MET-ONE**: MET-SOLE (it does not take one of several).
- **MET-EVERY, STEPS1-EVERY**: keep.
- **J-ONE-EACH**: the name contradicts its rule; fix the rule, then use J-EACH-PART.
- **"Carry"**: not one sense. It is a newborn's holdings, what a rule does, what a renaming does (SD's sense), FD's CARRY, and "carried on". Keep SD's and retitle: "What a newborn's holdings must depend on".
- **Also in the drafts**: "line", "side by side" and "beside" (D 0 bars them); "crosses" (D 0); "tells apart" (stem of "told"); "X counts" (see 15); and the new nouns "saturation" and "locality", against WD 0's "no new noun".

## 15. Scope and honesty

Scratch, as I would write it:

> In unreviewed scratch runs (five starts, 6 rounds, 800 knots, 153 of 156 items read), under rules that use no names and the recorded rations, the course from X only differed between two second parts in one case, and it differed just the same with both barred. Under the ordinary count with take-the-oldest it differed for every pair; that it differs under other numberings was checked for three pairs and nothing else was rechecked. Under one new ration it differed under parity, read for one round before the bound. In every case the two second parts come from start knots of different sizes, and no run separates "which part" from "how big its start knot was". No run tested that a difference went through the meeting.

Registered study, as I would write it:

> It would show whether, under a listed law, the course from X only differs with which of a small class it meets, and whether one value the law uses already separates them. It would not show a fold of emergence. The third property is untested, and where one value separates them the law, not the pattern, did it.

Blurs in the draft's sentence:
- "it was counting something the start had built": the take-every rule gave the places; no pattern counted.
- "through their meeting": untested.
- "the least a birth must carry is seen to be": from an ambiguous order, one class, and a confounded ration.

## 16. Verdict

Run the cheaper route of item 9 first, under its own short frozen text, and design the rest on its result. Do not freeze as it is.

Required, in order:
1. The class with Y's start knot fixed (h by acting members); barred-both retired to a report.
2. Attribution of the first differing used value as a condition of W; sealed run dropped; implied flag and guard in the used values.
3. Route 9 as set disjointness over every numbering by orbits, with all verdict parts.
4. Every law decided; the list of 78 written out; minimal laws reported; removals disclosed.
5. Controls for PARENT-OWING (constant 2; max(1, o); guard ×1, ×10, ×100), with the limits written.
6. Lemmas A, P and L corrected; the brief's L2 restored as the "composed" verdict of item 2(b).
7. Positive, planted and negative controls; the per-law list of which Y_h make a birth; a hand-listed gate.
8. The reader test of item 3 registered; the owner asked about MET-EVERY.
9. Definitions and words of items 11 and 14; caps by counts, not seconds.

Optional:
- the every-choice class, after a count of its histories;
- the stronger lasting test of item 1;
- a selector by fewest holders;
- made-7 to made-9.
